name: What is the difference between retail build-out and tenant improvement?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between retail build-out and tenant improvement in commercial construction?
mainEntity.text: What is the difference between retail build-out and tenant improvement in commercial construction?

acceptedAnswer.text: Retail build-out and tenant improvement are closely related terms, but they are not identical. Tenant improvement refers to any modifications made to leased commercial space to suit a tenant’s needs. Retail build-out is a type of tenant improvement specifically designed for a store, showroom, or customer-facing sales space. In practice, retail build-outs usually focus on finishes, merchandising layout, lighting, checkout areas, dressing rooms, and customer flow. The distinction matters when discussing budgets, leases, and contractor proposals, because some documents use the terms interchangeably while others use them more narrowly. Retail owners should make sure the scope matches the concept, rather than assuming a general tenant improvement allowance will cover a specialty retail space.
acceptedAnswer.description: A retail build-out is the construction process of turning a space into a functioning store. Tenant improvement is the broader term for improvements made to leased commercial space, which can include retail, office, restaurant, or medical projects.
